clue.text: Revenue from popular show

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to show up is to come, to arrive

explanation.surface: A theatre producer counting the takings from a hit show.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is money coming in, the same thing as revenue for a business or government.

clue.text: A blue, one doing badly

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: done badly means done wrong, so the letters of the verb come out in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Feeling blue, someone who is struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigo is a deep violet-blue colour, so it is one example of a blue.

clue.text: Italian must go after fall — don't be ridiculous!

indicators.note: going after means following, so this piece is placed at the end

parts.note: to come off a horse or bike is to fall
IT is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: An Italian being told to follow the autumn sounds absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Come off it is a colloquial retort meaning stop talking nonsense.

clue.text: Farmer George's combine

indicators.note: the apostrophe s stands for has, so the two names have the word held within them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A farmer called George owns a combine harvester.
explanation.walkthrough: Combine looks like the farm machine, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge things is to join them together into one, which is to combine them.

clue.text: Duck — child's toy duck is lost

indicators.note: something that is lost goes missing, so one letter drops out of the toy's name

parts.note: a two-wheeled toy a child pushes along with one foot
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A child loses a toy duck, as the dash lets the opening word sound like an anxious aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck appears twice: first as the bird defined, then as the cricket zero removed from the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: The scoter is a dark sea duck found off northern coasts, so it is one particular kind of duck.

clue.text: Professional jester nervous of our clot

indicators.note: nervous suggests jittery and unsettled, so the letters shake into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A paid comedian is wary of a fool among us.
explanation.definitionFit: A court fool was a jester employed at a royal court, paid to amuse the monarch.

clue.text: Pay for another in Italian restaurant when last of lasagne's eaten

indicators.note: something eaten is taken inside, so the letter goes within the restaurant's name

parts.note: trat is short for trattoria, a simple Italian restaurant

indicators.note: last of keeps only the final letter of the pasta dish

parts.note: final letter of lasagne

explanation.surface: Picking up the bill for a friend at the trattoria after the lasagne is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone is to pay for their meal or entertainment yourself.

clue.text: Give an account of most of red wine

indicators.note: most of means all but a little, so the final letter of the colour is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
port is a fortified wine from Portugal

explanation.surface: Describing a bottle of red wine after most of it has been drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: To report something is to describe it or give an account of it.

clue.text: Editor returned, brought back strange object

indicators.note: returned means going back the way it came, so the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: ED is the usual short form for editor

indicators.note: brought back means carried backwards, so this word is also read in reverse order

parts.note: rum means strange or odd in British slang

explanation.surface: An editor comes back from somewhere carrying an odd artefact.
explanation.walkthrough: Object looks like a noun in the surface, but it is the verb. Rum, meaning odd, is old-fashioned British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance, so it works as the verb object.

clue.text: Cut the mustard in test on horseback

parts.note: to measure something is to test or gauge it
a jockey riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: A rider proving their worth in an equestrian trial.
explanation.walkthrough: Racing reports say a jockey is up on a horse, which gives the short final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for being good enough or meeting the required standard.

clue.text: Noblewoman demonstrates about one working on Sunday

indicators.note: about means around, so the protest verb surrounds the next two pieces

parts.note: protesters march when they demonstrate
Roman numeral one
a machine that is on is working
S is the abbreviation for Sunday

explanation.surface: A protester complains about having to work on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so the Sunday letter comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is the wife of a marquess or a woman holding that rank, so a noblewoman.

clue.text: Change involving chapter results in an argument

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the change holds the chapter letter inside it

parts.note: an alteration is a change
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: An editor's revision to a chapter sparks a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy dispute or quarrel, so it is an argument.

clue.text: Travel widely with bootleg rum across Turkey

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the shuffled letters stretch either side of the country's code
rum means odd or strange, so the letters of the word beside it are put in an odd order

parts.note: taken as written
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A smuggler moving illicit liquor across Turkey covers a lot of ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum looks like the smuggled spirit, but it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To globetrot is to travel all over the world, a lively verb for travelling widely.

clue.text: Master tactician's first in heavy defeat to be written about

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole combination is written back to front
in places that single letter inside the word for a heavy defeat

parts.note: a rout is an overwhelming defeat

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word tactician

parts.note: opening letter of tactician

explanation.surface: A chess master's tactics are written up after a crushing loss.
explanation.definitionFit: A master in the teaching sense is a tutor, someone who instructs pupils.

clue.text: Public outburst about the Royal Marines as well

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outburst wraps round the other two pieces

parts.note: a furore is an outbreak of public anger or excitement
taken as written
RM is the abbreviation for Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A public row about the Royal Marines, one more thing to complain of.
explanation.definitionFit: Furthermore and as well both add another point to what was already said.

clue.text: Peculiar red and orange instrument

indicators.note: peculiar means odd or strange, so the letters are set in an odd order

parts.note: the two colour words; and only joins them

explanation.surface: A strangely coloured red and orange musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, is a keyboard instrument sounded by vibrating reeds.

clue.text: Attention given to female in pub, one who talks incessantly

parts.note: to give an ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: in places the female pronoun inside the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A woman in a pub gets attention from a man who will not stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Earbash is Australian and British slang for talking at someone without pause.
explanation.definitionFit: An earbasher is someone who lectures or chatters at length, a person who talks incessantly.

clue.text: Rechabite offering support to great Queen

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball
taken as written
great in the sense of big or high
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A member of some sect pledging loyalty to a great queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rechabites were a biblical family who drank no wine; a nineteenth-century temperance society took their name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rechabite abstains from alcohol, which is exactly what a teetotaller does.

clue.text: Excursion party's come over from stand

parts.note: a trip is an excursion

indicators.note: to come over is to turn over, so the party word flips round

parts.note: a do is a party; the 's is short for has

explanation.surface: Members of an outing come over from a stall or grandstand.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged stand for a camera or telescope.

clue.text: Iron clubs concealed by girl in grass

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: something concealed by another is hidden inside it, so the clubs letter goes within the girl's name

parts.note: a girl's name
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A girl hides golf clubs in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a common tufted grass used in lawns and pasture.

clue.text: Boy has to perform a musical composition

parts.note: a boy's name
to do is to perform an action

explanation.surface: A boy is required to play a piece of music, perhaps at a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning between contrasting sections.

clue.text: Turned up in honour of Tantalus's daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour awarded by the monarch

explanation.surface: Someone appearing at a ceremony to honour a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the word in is turned; the honour follows unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Niobe was a daughter of Tantalus whose children were slain, leaving her weeping into stone.

clue.text: Murder in the Spanish Main — it worried expedition's leader

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: worried means agitated or shaken about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of expedition

explanation.surface: A killing on a pirate voyage across the Spanish Main troubles the expedition's captain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish Main was the Caribbean coast of the old Spanish empire, so 'the Spanish Main' reads as one place but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliminate is a euphemism for kill, so it substitutes for the verb murder.

clue.text: Incensed upright character, judge

parts.note: the letter I is a single upright stroke
to rate something is to judge its worth

explanation.surface: An honest person is furious with a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: Upright character suggests an honest person, but it is the letter shaped like a vertical line.
explanation.definitionFit: Incensed and irate both mean very angry.

clue.text: Harrow boy makes laborious progress

parts.note: a harrow and a plough are both farm implements for breaking up the soil
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A pupil at Harrow, the English public school, slogging through his work.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow School is a famous English boarding school, but here harrow is the farm tool; the letters then regroup as a verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough on is an idiom for keeping going doggedly despite difficulty.

clue.text: A duke has acquired endless wine for this special purpose

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the last letter of the wine is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke
hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A duke has bought wine for a particular occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc is Latin for 'for this', describing something arranged only for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Expected girl to return with chaperone

parts.note: due means expected, as a train is due

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is due back home accompanied by her chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman who watches over a young lady, especially in Spain, which is a chaperone.

clue.text: Tries starter of estate car

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case in court

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: opening letter of estate

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to start an estate car, a British station wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estate car' looks like one unit, the British term for a station wagon, but the definition is car alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearse is the car that carries a coffin at a funeral.
